paper.title: GW150914: First results from the search for binary black hole coalescence with Advanced LIGO
paper.authors: LIGO Scientific Collaboration and Virgo Collaboration

thesis: A matched-filter search across both Advanced LIGO detectors identifies GW150914 as a highly significant binary-black-hole coalescence while retaining a second candidate as lower confidence.

nodes.title: Does O1 contain compact-binary signals?
nodes.body: Search Advanced LIGO observations for gravitational waves from binary black-hole coalescences and quantify background significance.

nodes.title: Matched-filter the detector streams
nodes.body: Compare strain data against relativistic compact-binary waveform templates and estimate noise background with time shifts.

nodes.title: Both detectors see a consistent transient
nodes.body: The Livingston and Hanford instruments recorded compatible waveforms separated by about seven milliseconds, within the inter-site light-travel time.

nodes.title: Network SNR is 24
nodes.body: The recovered event has a combined matched-filter signal-to-noise ratio of 24.

nodes.title: Background probability is negligible
nodes.body: The estimated false-alarm rate is below one event per 203,000 years, corresponding to significance above 5.1 sigma.

nodes.title: GW150914 is an astrophysical merger
nodes.body: The signal is consistent with coalescence of black holes of roughly 36 and 29 solar masses.

nodes.title: LVT151012 remains a weak branch
nodes.body: A second candidate has SNR 9.6, false-alarm rate about one per 2.3 years and p-value 0.02, so it is not promoted to a confident detection.

nodes.title: Separate detection from candidate
nodes.body: Treat GW150914 as a detection and LVT151012 as a lower-significance candidate based on the same background-calibrated search.

openQuestions: Detector calibration and waveform artifacts are referenced by the paper but not bundled in this compact fixture.
